name: dispatch-reconciliation
question: Of the dispatches this project logged that did NOT carry a submission receipt, which ones show the target taking a turn afterwards -- and which are still sitting with no sign of life, on a target that is still running?

assertion.asserts: no prompt dispatched to a live peer is stranded un-submitted in that peer's composer without anyone noticing
assertion.measures: for each non-confirmed entry in .claude/session-state/dispatch-log.jsonl within the lookback window, whether the target's .claude/session-state/turn-state/<resolvedId>.json carries a stamp whose atEpoch is greater than the dispatch's logged ts
known_gaps: THE central gap, and the reason the verdict is named ACTIVITY-AFTER-DISPATCH rather than CONFIRMED-LATE: turn-state stores only the target's LATEST transition, so a stamp newer than the dispatch proves the target took *a* turn afterwards -- never that the turn was ours. A user typing something unrelated in that window is textually indistinguishable from consumption of the dispatched prompt. The originating brief (DEFER-058) proposed CONFIRMED-LATE; that label would have asserted more than this measurement can support, so it was deliberately not adopted. Read ACTIVITY-AFTER-DISPATCH as 'consistent with consumption', never as proof of it

the converse under-report: a target that consumed the prompt, finished, and had its Stop hook FAIL leaves turn-active frozen at an old timestamp. That target reads as NO-ACTIVITY-SINCE and can be graded a false stranding. The DISPATCH-11 stale-turn caveat names the same hazard at dispatch time; neither surface can resolve it from the stamp alone

a target whose prompt was genuinely stranded but which the user then rescued by hand (pressing Enter) reads as ACTIVITY-AFTER-DISPATCH and is graded pass. That is the correct OUTCOME but the wrong REASON -- the oracle cannot see that a human closed the loop, so it cannot count how often the Human-as-I/O-Relay path is still being walked

FAIL is deliberately restricted to a four-way conjunction (reason == receipt-timeout AND in-window AND target still live AND no activity since). Every other stranded-looking row is reported informationally. This means a genuinely stranded prompt on a target that has since EXITED is never graded fail -- correctly, since nothing can be done about it, but it also means the fail count systematically under-reports historical stranding. The count is an actionability measure, not an incidence measure

`delivered-queued` entries (DISPATCH-11: the target was mid-turn) are reconciled and reported but NEVER graded fail, because a non-receipt from a busy target is the expected result rather than a symptom. If the queued classification itself were wrong -- a stale turn-active stamp misread as genuine work -- this oracle would inherit that error silently and report the row as merely informational

the log records the dispatch's ts at SECOND granularity and the turn-state stamp likewise, so a target that submits within the same second as the dispatch is compared with a strictly-greater test and can read as NO-ACTIVITY-SINCE. In practice the receipt path inside the dispatcher already catches that case as CONFIRMED, so it reaches this oracle only when the receipt poll was skipped or raced

scope is one project's log. A cross-project dispatch (--project=<path>) logs into the TARGET project's session-state, so reconciling it means running this oracle THERE. Running it here will not see it, and will not say so -- absence of a row is indistinguishable from a dispatch that was never sent

liveness is read from the registry plus a PID check. A registry entry that is stale in the optimistic direction (recorded PID belongs to a recycled process) makes a dead target look live and can produce a false fail

cost_provenance: measured 2026-08-02 on the ULDF framework repo: the dominant cost is one pass over dispatch-log.jsonl plus one small file read per distinct target. Declared pessimistically at 2500ms per ORACLE-COST-01 because the log is append-only and unbounded -- a project with a very long dispatch history pays linearly in the scan, and under-declaration causes timeout kills

schema.status: string -- pass | fail | no-data. fail ONLY on the four-way conjunction described in known_gaps

details.entries_scanned: integer -- non-confirmed entries inside the lookback window
details.stranded_actionable: integer -- the fail count; the four-way conjunction
details.contract: string -- the standing over-claim disclaimer, emitted on every run

entries.ts: string -- ISO8601-UTC, when the dispatch was logged
entries.target: string -- the id as typed by the caller
entries.resolvedId: string -- the id receipts and turn-state key on
entries.actionable: boolean -- true only for rows that count toward status=fail
entries.stampAt: string -- the target's latest turn-state stamp, or empty
